countries.summary: Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap (launched 30 May 2024) sets the national direction: at least 300 MW of added capacity, with more if the capacity runs on green energy, and a PUE target of 1.3 or lower. Capacity is released through the DC-CFA competitive calls already in the dataset. AWS has committed S$12 billion more to its Singapore cloud infrastructure through 2028. This pass verified two new records and two context facts from secondary-law-firm and company/EDB pages; the IMDA pages probed were JavaScript shells with no body text, so no IMDA-authored quote is cited.

regulators.name: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA)
regulators.notes: Probed (HTTP 200). Page is a script-rendered shell; the roadmap is confirmed only through the Mayer Brown quotes. Co-owner of the Green Data Centre Roadmap and the BCA-IMDA Green Mark for Data Centres.

regulators.name: Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB)
regulators.notes: Probed (HTTP 200, page updated 19 Oct 2026). Publishes investment announcements and the DC-CFA allocation context.

context.statement: Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap was launched on 30 May 2024 with a target of at least 300 MW of additional data-centre capacity, with further capacity if green energy is used.
context.verbatim: Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap (GDCR) was launched on 30 May 2024 by the Singapore Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), along with the announcement that Singapore aims to provide at least 300 megawatts of additional capacity for data centres and further additional capacity if green energy is used.
context.source_title: Mayer Brown — Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap (Aug 2024)

context.statement: The IMDA has set a target for data centres to reach a PUE of 1.3 or lower at 100% IT load over the next 10 years.
context.verbatim: The IMDA has set a target for data centres to achieve a Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of less than or equal to 1.3 at 100% IT load over the next 10 years.
context.source_title: Mayer Brown — Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap (Aug 2024)
context.notes: Secondary law-firm summary of the IMDA roadmap. The IMDA factsheet PDF (mddi.gov.sg) returned 404 and the IMDA page is a script shell, so the primary text was not reachable.

context.statement: The BCA-IMDA Green Mark Data Centre Platinum certification is named as a best-in-class energy-efficiency benchmark that EDB and IMDA give as an example of performance.
context.verbatim: including meeting the Green Mark DC Platinum Certification (see note 6 below on the BCA-IMDA Green Mark for Data Centres)
context.source_title: Mayer Brown — Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap (Aug 2024)
context.notes: Mayer Brown describes the Green Mark as a rating scheme that the IMDA will refresh. Context only, not a standalone policy record.

countries.summary: Alberta's large-load rules now have two layers. A one-time AESO interim stage of 1,200 MW is fully allocated, and the June 2026 Data Centre Regulation directs the AESO to prioritize projects that bring dedicated new generation or storage. Quebec's Hydro-Quebec has proposed a data-centre rate averaging about 13 cents per kWh (rate case R-4333-2026, still pending), and Microsoft's US$500 million Quebec build targets the Lévis area. This pass verified four new or updated records, but the Alberta Wonder Valley status and the Quebec Régie regulator page could not be verified (the Régie site returned 403).

regulators.name: Alberta Electric System Operator (AESO)
regulators.notes: Probed (HTTP 200). Runs the Alberta grid and the large-load connection list. The Phase 2 framework is being finalized.

regulators.name: Régie de l'énergie du Québec
regulators.notes: Hearing docket R-4333-2026 for the Hydro-Quebec large data-centre rate. The regie-energie.qc.ca homepage returned 403 to probe, so no URL is stored; the Hydro-Quebec release on the rate is cited instead.

context.statement: Companies have asked to connect roughly 19,565 MW of new data-centre load in Alberta, far more than the AESO allowed onto the grid in its first stage.
context.verbatim: Companies have asked to connect roughly 19,565 megawatts of new data centre load, far more than the AESO allowed onto the grid in this first stage.
context.source_title: Government of Alberta — Is Alberta's grid ready?
context.notes: Government messaging page citing the AESO connection list dated 30 July 2026 (figure moves quarterly). The page's own framing should be read as government position.

countries.summary: Chile's tribunal and environmental-permit path decides data-centre projects site by site. The Segundo Tribunal Ambiental rejected a neighbour's challenge to Amazon Web Services' Huechuraba storage centre on 31 March 2026, after the SEA approved it in 2024 and a related claim was dismissed in 2025. The Cerrillos court judgment is already in the dataset (its own tribunal page was not located). This pass verified one project and one response for Chile; the SEA homepage was probed as the regulator.

regulators.name: Servicio de Evaluación Ambiental (SEA)
regulators.notes: Probed (HTTP 200). Runs environmental impact assessments (DIA/EIA) and issues the RCA; the Huechuraba project was approved through this channel.

countries.summary: Argentina's big data-centre case is Stargate Argentina, announced in October 2025 as a 500 MW renewable-powered campus in Patagonia, with a letter of intent between OpenAI and Sur Energy. The project is to be routed through the RIGI regime. This pass verified the announcement from regional press only: no official Casa Rosada or OpenAI statement was reachable (openai.com returned 403), and no RIGI approval for a data centre was found in the sources checked.

Sweden's largest verified data-centre fights are about grid capacity rather than heat: Brookfield's planned 750 MW AI campus at Strängnäs faces a grid-reinforcement application that Svenska kraftnät says has only partly arrived. atNorth's SWE02 in Kista is designed to hand excess heat to Stockholm's district heating in collaboration with Stockholm Exergi. This pass verified three SE records. The Stockholm Exergi heat terms and the Ei consultation were not verified, and Ei's own domain returned an SSL error to probe.

regulators.name: Svenska kraftnät
regulators.notes: Probed (HTTP 200). Swedish transmission system operator. It pays for transmission reinforcements and is assessing the Strängnäs request.

regulators.name: Energimarknadsinspektionen (Ei)
regulators.notes: Existing record. The energimarknadsinspektionen.se probe failed on an SSL certificate mismatch, so no URL is stored.

countries.summary: Finland's grid is absorbing large data-centre demand: Fingrid's half-year 2026 report says over 3 GW of data-centre capacity has signed connection agreements. Two hyperscale or large sites are in development: Google's Muhos campus (in preliminary construction, permits stated) and XTX Markets' Kajaani complex, which plans heat supply to the town. This pass verified four Finnish records and one context fact.

regulators.name: Fingrid
regulators.notes: Probed (HTTP 200). Finland's transmission operator; its half-year 2026 report is the source for the connection-agreement figure.

context.statement: Planned data-centre capacity with signed connection agreements at Fingrid exceeded 3 GW by the end of June 2026.
context.verbatim: the planned total capacity of data centre projects that have signed connection agreements by the end of June was over three gigawatts.
context.notes: Figure is Fingrid's and is based on information provided by project parties. Fingrid also reports about 50 new connection agreements in 12 months, around a third for data centres.

fields.title: Green Data Centre Roadmap (IMDA, 2024)
fields.summary: National roadmap launched 30 May 2024 that sets green data-centre standards (energy efficiency at facility and IT level, green energy, water efficiency) and a capacity direction of at least 300 MW of additional capacity, with more if green energy is used. Sets a PUE target of 1.3 or lower at 100% IT load over 10 years.
key_terms: at least 300 megawatts of additional capacity
Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of less than or equal to 1.3

records.source_title: Mayer Brown — Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap (Aug 2024)
records.verbatim: Singapore aims to provide at least 300 megawatts of additional capacity for data centres and further additional capacity if green energy is used. The IMDA has set a target for data centres to achieve a Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of less than or equal to 1.3 at 100% IT load over the next 10 years.
records.notes: Secondary (law firm) source; the IMDA factsheet and roadmap PDF were not reachable by probe. Both sentences probe-HIT on the Mayer Brown page. Principles are a curator judgment. The roadmap is a framework, not a binding community-benefit instrument, so community_benefits_framework is false.

fields.statement: At the 10th AWS ASEAN Summit in Singapore today, Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced plans to invest an additional S$12 billion into its existing cloud infrastructure in Singapore from 2024 to 2028 to meet growing customer demand for cloud technology and services in the country.

records.source_title: Singapore EDB — AWS to invest an additional SG$12 billion in Singapore by 2028, and announces flagship AI programme
records.verbatim: At the 10th AWS ASEAN Summit in Singapore today, Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced plans to invest an additional S$12 billion into its existing cloud infrastructure in Singapore from 2024 to 2028 to meet growing customer demand for cloud technology and services in the country.
records.notes: Joint AWS/Amazon release reproduced on the EDB site, so first-party to AWS. Announced May 2024. The EDB page includes an AWS economic-impact study estimate (S$23.7 billion GDP contribution, 12,300 jobs), which is AWS's own figure and not verified here as a standalone claim. Probe matched the sentence.

fields.summary: Hydro-Québec's February 2026 proposal sets a new large data-centre rate (projects above 5 MW) equivalent to an average of 13 cents per kWh, approximately double what current large-power customers pay. Expected to take effect in the second half of 2026, subject to Régie approval. Existing grid-connected data centres would get a transitional rate.

records.source_title: Hydro-Québec — A new rate for data centres and a rate adjustment for blockchains to reflect the value of renewable electricity (19 Feb 2026)
records.verbatim: which is equivalent to an average of 13¢/kWh, approximately double what current large-power customers pay. The rate is expected to take effect in the second half of 2026, subject to approval by the Régie de l'énergie.
records.notes: Utility's own press release (first-party to Hydro-Québec). Probe matched both sentences. The Régie decision had not been found as of the sources checked; the record stays pending. The 5 MW threshold sentence also probe-HIT ('data centres requiring a capacity greater than 5 MW'). The Hydro-Québec block allocation (300 MW AI / 100 MW other) was seen only in search and a filing, so it is not included.

fields.title: Alberta Data Centre Regulation (June 2026)
fields.summary: Regulation in force since June 2026 that directs the AESO to prioritize data-centre connection requests tied to dedicated new generation or storage. Per a law-firm note cited by the government page, it also gives the AESO discretion to set criteria (e.g. municipal zoning approvals). The regulation's own text was not fetched; its citation number is not verified.
key_terms: prioritize projects tethered to dedicated new generation or storage

records.source_title: Government of Alberta — Is Alberta's grid ready?
records.verbatim: The Data Centre Regulation (June 2026) directs the AESO to prioritize projects tethered to dedicated new generation or storage.
records.notes: Source is the government's own explainer page, not the regulation text. Confirm the Alberta Regulation citation on the Alberta King's Printer site before shipping. The statutory citation is left null.

fields.title: AESO stage-one interim large-load allocation (1,200 MW)
fields.summary: AESO's one-time interim limit of 1,200 MW for new large data-centre load, the first stage of Alberta's large-load connection rules. The government page says this stage is now fully allocated, and that the permanent Phase 2 framework is being finalized.

records.source_title: Government of Alberta — Is Alberta's grid ready?
records.verbatim: The amount the AESO allowed to connect, now fully allocated.
records.notes: The 1,200 MW figure is probe-matched on the same page ('set an interim limit of 1,200 megawatts'). The date is not stated on the page and is left null. Government messaging page, cross-check with AESO before shipping.

fields.name: Microsoft Québec data centres (Québec-Lévis economic zone)
fields.notes: Announced November 2023 as four data centres in the Québec City region (L'Ancienne-Lorette, Donnacona, Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, Lévis) per other reports; only the Lévis location is probe-matched. Coordinates are the Lévis municipal centre (Wikipedia), not a site address. Construction status not verified.

records.source_title: BetaKit — Microsoft looks to scale Québec presence with $500-million USD investment
records.verbatim: Microsoft is betting big on Québec as the tech giant earmarks $685 million CAD ($500 million USD) to expand its cloud computing and AI infrastructure in the province over the next two years.
records.notes: Secondary press (BetaKit, 22 Nov 2023). The Lévis location sentence ('By choosing to locate in the Québec-Lévis economic zone, Microsoft is sending a strong message...') is a quote from a Québec minister, not from Microsoft. The Microsoft newsroom release was not reachable. Other named municipalities were not probe-matched.

fields.title: BCA-IMDA Green Mark for Data Centres
fields.summary: Certification scheme that awards data-centre operators that deploy green data-centre best practices and demonstrate superior energy and environmental performance. Platinum (DC) is the top tier that EDB and IMDA cite as an example of best-in-class efficiency.

records.source_title: Mayer Brown — Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap (Aug 2024)
records.verbatim: including meeting the Green Mark DC Platinum Certification (see note 6 below on the BCA-IMDA Green Mark for Data Centres)
records.notes: Secondary source. Probe matched. Certification scheme, not a legal instrument. Scheme description text ('a certification rating scheme awarding operators...') was also probe-matched on the same page. Add the BCA page as a primary source before shipping.

fields.name: Brookfield AI data centre, Strängnäs
fields.notes: Planned capacity stated as 750 MW in the SVT report (up from a 300 MW plan). Coordinates are the Strängnäs town centre (Wikipedia), not the site. A 2025 listing places the site at Gorsingeberget (E20), not verified against a planning document. No 2026 zoning decision or grid agreement found. SE-04 is the ISO code for Södermanland; verify the subdivision code before shipping.

records.source_title: SVT Nyheter Sörmland — Lokala kraftnätet klarar inte enorma AI-satsningen i Strängnäs (8 Jun 2025)
records.verbatim: Med en planerad investering på hela 95 miljarder kronor vill det kanadensiska bolaget Brookfield Asset Management göra Strängnäs till norra Europas största centrum för AI-produktion.
records.translation: With a planned investment of as much as 95 billion kronor, the Canadian company Brookfield Asset Management wants to make Strängnäs the largest centre for AI production in northern Europe.
records.notes: Publication date 8 June 2025 is on the page. The 95 billion kronor sentence and the 750 MW sentence (in the response record) both probe-HIT. The 300 to 750 MW expansion is from a secondary search summary, not probe-matched, so the record uses 750 MW only as the page states it.

fields.summary: Svenska kraftnät's grid-development manager says the 750 MW load is far too large for the local grid and that reinforcements are needed. He confirms the Brookfield grid application reached the TSO only in part, and that the TSO would pay for transmission-level reinforcement. The grid operator is assessing the request; this is a technical statement, not an objection.

records.source_title: SVT Nyheter Sörmland — Lokala kraftnätet klarar inte enorma AI-satsningen i Strängnäs (8 Jun 2025)
records.verbatim: 750 megawatt är en alldeles för stor belastning för det lokala kraftnätet. Där behövs förstärkningar, säger Tobias Edfast, sektionschef för nätutveckling på Svenska kraftnät.
records.translation: 750 megawatts is a far too large load for the local grid. Reinforcements are needed, says Tobias Edfast, section manager for grid development at Svenska kraftnät.
records.notes: Constituency is 'regulator' by the schema list, but Svenska kraftnät is the transmission operator, not the energy regulator. Use the grid-operator statement as a technical response only. The 750 MW sentence and 'Där behövs förstärkningar' both probe-HIT. The leading dash in the page text is dropped from the verbatim.

fields.name: atNorth SWE02 (Kista)
fields.notes: 30 MW metro data centre per other reports of the atNorth release (the '30 MW' phrase did not probe-match on the newsroom page, so power is left null). Operator is not a tracked company. Heat reuse to Stockholm district heating is with Stockholm Exergi. Coordinates not probed. Ellevio substation claim from Converge Digest only; not used. Go-live Q4 2027 per release. Date 29 Jan 2026 per trade press.

records.source_title: atNorth — New 30MW metro data center in Stockholm, Sweden
records.verbatim: It will be enabled with heat reuse capabilities, allowing excess heat from the data center to be recovered and recycled for use within the local community, in collaboration with Stockholm Exergi.
records.notes: Company release (first-party to atNorth). The Q4 2027 go-live sentence ('The site is scheduled to go live in Q4 2027.') also probe-HIT. The Stockholm Exergi heat-supply contract terms were not found, so the record claims collaboration only, not a signed heat price or volume. Subdivision SE-01 is the Stockholm county code; verify before shipping.

fields.statement: It will be enabled with heat reuse capabilities, allowing excess heat from the data center to be recovered and recycled for use within the local community, in collaboration with Stockholm Exergi.

records.source_title: atNorth — New 30MW metro data center in Stockholm, Sweden
records.verbatim: It will be enabled with heat reuse capabilities, allowing excess heat from the data center to be recovered and recycled for use within the local community, in collaboration with Stockholm Exergi.
records.notes: First-party atNorth statement, same release as the SWE02 project record. Stockholm Exergi executive quote on the same page ('We are proud to collaborate with atNorth to recycle heat to meet a local need within Stockholm') is also probe-HIT and could be a second claim.

fields.name: XTX Markets Kajaani data centre complex
fields.notes: First data centre: three data halls totalling 22.5 MW of IT power (not grid capacity, so power_mw is left null), 15,000 m2, on a 478-acre site. Four further data centres planned. Operator is not a tracked company. Construction underway as of the Jan 2025 release, with completion planned for 2026. Coordinates are Kajaani town (Wikipedia), not the site.

records.source_title: XTX Markets — Press release: XTX Markets plans to invest over €1bn in large-scale data centre project in Finland (22 Jan 2025)
records.verbatim: London / Kajaani, 22nd January 2025-XTX Markets today announced plans to invest over €1bn to develop a state-of-the-art data centre complex in Kajaani, Finland.
records.notes: Operator's own press release. The 22.5 MW IT figure ('three data halls totalling 22.5MW of IT power') was probe-matched on the same page. Status 'construction' comes from the release, not a 2026 progress check.

fields.statement: XTX Markets is exploring ways that the heat generated by the data centre can be provided free of charge to the local community of Kajaani and reduce the facility's environmental footprint.

records.source_title: XTX Markets — Press release: XTX Markets plans to invest over €1bn in large-scale data centre project in Finland (22 Jan 2025)
records.verbatim: XTX Markets is exploring ways that the heat generated by the data centre can be provided free of charge to the local community of Kajaani and reduce the facility's environmental footprint.
records.notes: Exploratory wording: no heat-supply agreement is stated. Probe matched the full sentence on the operator release.

fields.name: Google Muhos data centre
fields.notes: Google's own site page (dated September 2026) says site activity is limited to preliminary infrastructure development, with the next construction phase being prepared. Google's Kajaani and Muhos land holding is 1,400 ha for EUR 27m per a secondary report, not verified here. No MW figure found. Coordinates are Muhos town (Wikipedia), not the site.

records.verbatim: All work is proceeding in full compliance with obtained permits.
records.notes: Google first-party page, probe-matched 'SEPTEMBER 2026' page text. The 'in development' label and the preliminary infrastructure wording are on the same page. The page describes a waste-heat and circular-economy plan (see claim record).

fields.statement: we power local industries by capturing and recycling waste heat

records.verbatim: we power local industries by capturing and recycling waste heat
records.notes: Google first-party page. The statement is cut to the probe-matched clause; the longer sentence ('showcasing a commitment to the circular economy') did not probe-match and is omitted. Waste-heat use is a Google plan at a site in development, not a delivered service.

fields.name: AWS Huechuraba storage data centre (Centro de Almacenamiento Huechuraba)
fields.operator: Amazon Web Services (Servicios Amazon Data Services Chile SpA)
fields.notes: Environmentally approved by the Región Metropolitana evaluation commission on 12 July 2024 (per press, SEA record not fetched). Site 10.9 ha, 21,350 m2 built area, 30-year design life per press. Phase 1 construction was reported to begin Dec 2025, but no 2026 construction confirmation was found, so the status stays 'announced'. Coordinates not probed. Power, water and generator figures are press-reported and not used.

records.source_title: Forbes Chile — Justicia ambiental da luz verde al proyecto de data center de Amazon en Huechuraba (6 Apr 2026)
records.verbatim: Este proyecto en particular supone una inversión de 205 millones de dólares
records.translation: This particular project represents an investment of 205 million dollars.
records.notes: Secondary press (Forbes Chile). The court-ruling sentence is probe-matched in the response record. Use the SEA expediente (SEIA) before shipping; the SEIA page was not reachable through search. The 205 million figure is from press, not an AWS release.

fields.project: AWS Huechuraba storage data centre (Centro de Almacenamiento Huechuraba)
fields.summary: A neighbour's administrative claim against the environmental approval, arguing the data centre was improperly split from a high-voltage line project, was dismissed by the Segundo Tribunal Ambiental in a ruling of 31 March 2026. The court found no basis for treating the two as one project.

records.source_title: Forbes Chile — Justicia ambiental da luz verde al proyecto de data center de Amazon en Huechuraba (6 Apr 2026)
records.verbatim: El Segundo Tribunal Ambiental informó que tras analizar el reclamo de que el Centro de Almacenamiento se relacionaba con la construcción de una Línea de Alta Tensión Huechuraba, este fue desestimado.
records.translation: The Segundo Tribunal Ambiental reported that, after analysing the claim that the storage centre was linked to construction of the Huechuraba high-voltage line, the claim was dismissed.
records.notes: Probe matched 'este fue desestimado' on the Forbes page. The ruling date 31 de marzo is probe-matched on the same page. Stance is negative because it is a neighbour's objection; the outcome (dismissed) is in the summary. Single neighbour, not a community movement.

records.locality: Patagonia (Neuquén, Río Negro or Chubut candidate provinces)

fields.name: Stargate Argentina (Sur Energy, OpenAI offtake)

claimed_investment.as_stated: entre US$20.000 y US$25.000 millones (range, low end shown)

fields.notes: Letter of intent between OpenAI and Sur Energy, presented to President Milei on 9 Oct 2025 (per press). Planned 500 MW of renewable-powered capacity; construction said to start in 2026, first 100 MW operating around end-2027. Sur Energy's chief said in Nov 2025 it expects to activate the Patagonian data centres in 2027. RIGI registration status not confirmed; no RIGI approval for a data centre found in the sources checked. Operator Sur Energy is not a tracked company. The OpenAI global-affairs page returned 403 to probe, so no first-party OpenAI quote is cited. Investment range upper bound US$25bn; the record keeps the low end, and the range is in as_stated.

records.source_title: NoticiasNQN — OpenAI y Sur Energy construirán un megacentro de datos para inteligencia artificial en la Patagonia (10 Oct 2025)
records.verbatim: un centro de datos de 500 MW alimentado con energía renovable
records.translation: a 500 MW data centre powered by renewable energy
records.notes: Regional press (NoticiasNQN, 10 Oct 2025), secondary to the government and OpenAI announcements, which were not reachable. Probe matched the 500 MW phrase. The investment range is probe-matched in the article text but not as a single exact phrase; the as_stated field holds the article's words. Province AR-U is a placeholder and is not verified: the article does not name a province. Replace with the verified province (or null) before shipping, and set the subdivision accordingly.
